newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WITNESS IN GROBBELAAR CASE TO BE TRIED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WITNESS IN GROBBELAAR CASE TO BE TRIED.

text.p: The chief prosecution witness in the trial of goalkeeper Bruce Grobbelaar and two other star soccer players will stand trial charged with attempting to pervert the course of justice, a British judge said on Friday.
Vincent, a 38-year-old Zimbabwean businessman, is accused of offering not to appear as a witness in the Grobbelaar case in exchange for money.

A judge in Aldershot, southern England, where Vincent was arrested in October, ordered him to be tried for the alleged offence. He will be held in custody until his next court appearance on December 1.

Grobbelaar, who played for Southampton and Liverpool and now is with Plymouth, retired Aston Villa striker John Fashanu and Dutch-born Wimbledon goalkeeper Hans Seger are accused of giving and taking bribes to fix the result of matches.

They were charged after a police investigation prompted by media allegations about the activities of an Asian gambling syndicate in England. They are due to stand trial in January. Grobbelaar is accused of accepting 2,000 pounds ($3,300) from Vincent, his former business partner, in November 1994 for throwing an unspecified match.
